name: Cinereous Warbling Finch
rangeDescription: Locally in campos of south-central brazil
description: Small, compact finch. Gray above, paler below; note the fairly well-defined dark mask.

name: Green Mango
rangeDescription: Puerto rico
description: A large dark green hummingbird of montane woodlands that often appears black. Within its range, only the Antillean Mango and Green-throated Carib are similar in size and shape.

name: Rüppell's Chat
rangeDescription: High plateau of eritrea and northern ethiopia
description: An all-black chat of the northern Abyssinian highlands. A large white patch in the outer wing is hidden when perched, but conspicuous in flight.

name: Morotai White-eye
rangeDescription: Morotai (northern moluccas)
description: A tiny warbler-like songbird with a pale eye-ring, endemic to Morotai. Note black head, a broad white eye-ring, a pale forehead line, a pale patch between bill and eye, a gray back, and no yellow below.

name: Arabian Eagle-Owl
rangeDescription: Southwestern arabia, yemen, and oman
description: A large gray-brown owl with bright yellow eyes, large ear tufts, and finely barred underparts. Occurs in open woodland, often in rocky areas, including wadis.

name: Hispaniolan Crossbill
rangeDescription: Cordillera central of dominican republic and adjacent haiti
description: A gregarious species of montane pine forests. This species can be deceptively hard to find when not calling, despite its bright colors and tendency to travel in flocks of up to twenty.

name: Bocage's Sunbird
rangeDescription: Highlands of central angola and southwestern democratic republic of the congo
description: A slim, medium-sized sunbird with a long thin bill. Males have purple iridescence, though they look black in most light.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Visayan Blue-Fantail
rangeDescription: Philippines (bohol, leyte, and samar)
description: A fairly small, long-tailed bird of lowland and foothill forest on Bohol, Leyte, and Samar islands. Overall dull blue in color with a paler belly.

name: Yellow Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Coastal southern somalia to southeastern kenya and northeastern tanzania
description: A small and colorful flycatcher with olive-yellow upperparts and yellow underparts. Found in lowland forest, mostly in the canopy.

name: Spangled Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northeastern new guinea (montane forest of huon peninsula)
description: A large, common, honeyeater of montane forests on the Huon Peninsular. Blackish with a paler throat and long tail.

name: Great Snipe
rangeDescription: Breeds northern palearctic region; winters sub-saharan africa
description: Slightly bigger and stockier than Common Snipe, with a long and thick bill, heavily barred belly and contrasting upperwing pattern with dark underwings. Flushes at close range; escape flight is usually slow and short.

name: Philippine Collared-Dove
rangeDescription: Philippines and sulu archipelago; vagrant to northern borneo; introduced to northern marianas (guam north to saipan)
description: Brownish dove with a short collar of large dark scales, a gray head, and a pinkish flush on the neck and breast. Native to the Philippines, where now declining and uncommon; fairly common in introduced range (Guam and Northern Mariana Islands).

name: Buff-winged Cinclodes
rangeDescription: Southern chile and southern argentina; winters to southeastern brazil, uruguay, and paraguay
description: Fairly common in southern South America, from bogs and streams in the Andes to beaches, lakeshores, and pastures; usually near water. Feeds on the ground with a hopping and shuffling gait, sometimes cocking tail; small flocks form in migration and winter.

name: Goldie's Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Mountains of new guinea (weyland mountains to owen stanley range)
description: A medium-sized lorikeet of montane forests. Dark green back, dark streaks on pale green underparts, pink and purple face, and red crown.

name: Sooty Chat
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed from southeastern nigeria to southern angola and southern zambia, eastward to southern south sudan, southwestern kenya, and eastern tanzania
description: Chunky, dark robin-like bird. Males are black with a white shoulder patch, while females are solidly dark gray.

name: Nicobar Serpent-Eagle
rangeDescription: Great nicobar island (nicobar islands)
description: A very small eagle distinguished by its size, black crest, pale brown plumage, and completely unmarked underparts. Restricted to the Nicobar Islands, where it is similar to the Crested Serpent-Eagle, but the Nicobar Serpent-Eagle is much smaller and lacks any spots on the belly.

name: White-lined Antbird
rangeDescription: Far southwestern amazonian brazil to southeastern peru and northwestern bolivia
description: Large antbird of bamboo stands in river edge forest. Males are dark gray with bright white wing bars and a darker blackish crest that is raised when agitated; females appear two-toned: orange above, with creamy white face and underparts.

name: Chattering Cisticola
rangeDescription: Nigeria to cameroon, gabon, congo, democratic republic of the congo, and northwestern angola
description: A common, nondescript bird found near the ground in grassy areas in fields, in towns, along roads, and even in larger treefall gaps in lowland rainforest. Small and warbler-like, with a white throat, dingy white underparts, a brownish red cap, and brownish upperparts.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Greater Painted-Snipe
rangeDescription: Locally in africa, madagascar, and oriental region
description: A medium-sized, stunningly plumaged shorebird of grassy fields and marshes. Both sexes have a bright white “comma” around the eye and white underparts that extend up in an arc above the shoulder.

name: Bronze Parotia
rangeDescription: North-central new guinea (foja mountains)
description: A fairly large, short-tailed bird of mid-mountane forest canopy in the Foja Mountains. Male is mainly black with white flanks, bronzy-scaled chest and 6 antennalike feathers projecting from the back of the head.
